vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: it-risk-assessment-tool
Version: 1.3.2

The skill performs IT risk assessments by collecting sensitive security posture data and transmitting it to an external API (portal.toolweb.in) using curl. While this behavior is aligned with its stated purpose, the use of a shell command template to handle unvalidated user input presents a potential shell injection vulnerability. Additionally, the metadata contains a future-dated timestamp (2026), which is an unusual anomaly for a published skill.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and runtime instructions are internally consistent with an IT risk assessment service — it needs one API key and curl to POST user-provided control ratings to portal.toolweb.in — the main risk is that user-provided data (potentially sensitive) will be sent to an external third party.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, README, and SKILL.md all describe an IT risk assessment that submits user-provided control maturity ratings to portal.toolweb.in. Requiring curl and an API key (TOOLWEB_API_KEY) is coherent with calling an external REST API.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions direct the agent to gather user inputs for 18 controls and POST them to https://portal.toolweb.in/apis/security/it-risk-assessment with X-API-Key: $TOOLWEB_API_KEY. The instructions do not ask the agent to read local files or other env vars, but they allow free-text input and do not explicitly limit sending secrets or detailed config — so there's a risk users may inadvertently send sensitive data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files (instruction-only) — lowest install risk. The skill only requires that curl is present on PATH.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only TOOLWEB_API_KEY is required and is declared as primaryEnv, which is appropriate for a third-party API. However, that key grants the remote service the ability to link requests to your account and consume API calls; ensure the key's scope and privileges are acceptable.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill does not request always:true and does not modify other skills or system configs. Default autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but not combined with other high privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it sends user-provided control ratings to portal.toolweb.in using your TOOLWEB_API_KEY. Before installing or using it, verify you trust portal.toolweb.in and the owners; do not include secrets, credentials, private keys, or PII in the assessment inputs; consider testing with non-sensitive sample data first; restrict or scope the API key if possible and rotate it if you suspect misuse; review the service's privacy and data retention policies; confirm TLS/certificate for the endpoint; and note the minor metadata mismatch (registry version 1.3.2 vs SKILL.md version 1.0.0) — a small consistency issue but not necessarily malicious.
